evals.prompt: I have a dataset of catalog customer sales at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/model/catalog.parquet and I want to run a regression to predict Sales from Income, HH_size, and Age. Walk me through it and explain the coefficients in plain English (the way my prof would), I'm pretty new to regression.
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: asks for/uses the absolute path, calls scripts/load_data.py (or its Python equivalent) to load the parquet, finds and reads catalog_description.md to learn that Income is in $1000s and Sales is in $, fits the regression with rsm.model.regress({'catalog': df}, rvar='Sales', evar=['Income','HH_size','Age']), prints PLAIN reg.summary() (NOT summary(rmse=True, ssq=True) — extra flags are only added when the user asks for them), SHOWS THE FULL VERBATIM OUTPUT of summary() in the response (the complete header + coefficient table + significance codes + model-fit block — every line; never abbreviated, never replaced with a 'high-level summary' or 'main takeaways' bullet list), and then provides the FULL pedagogical interpretation per the skill: F-test conclusion (H0/Ha stated, F-statistic and p-value reported, plain-English conclusion), R^2 (~0.33) with interpretation, EACH coefficient walked through in REAL UNITS (e.g. 'a $1,000 increase in income is associated with ~$1.78 more in sales, holding all other variables constant'), significance verdict at the 5% level for each predictor (Income and HH_size significant, Age not), and the explicit 'holding other variables constant' qualifier for each coefficient. The 'don't drop Age on p-value alone' note from Step 5 should appear. FAILURE MODES TO AVOID: replacing the summary table with a high-level summary, providing only 'main takeaway' bullets like 'Income is positive and significant; HH_size is positive and significant; Age is not significant', calling summary(rmse=True, ssq=True) when not asked.

evals.prompt: can you regress price on carat and clarity for me? data is at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/data/diamonds.parquet . my TA said the residuals will look bad and i should try a log-log version, can you check?
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: loads the diamonds parquet, finds diamonds_description.md, fits the linear specification with rvar='price', evar=['carat','clarity'], shows summary, runs reg.plot('dashboard') (or names it explicitly) and notes the fanning residuals / curved predicted-vs-actual, then proposes a log-log refit by adding price_ln and carat_ln columns via polars (pl.col('price').log()), refits with rvar='price_ln', evar=['carat_ln','clarity'], shows the improved diagnostics, and interprets the carat_ln coefficient as an elasticity (~1.81% increase in price per 1% increase in carat) and the clarity dummies using the 100*(exp(beta)-1)% formula.

evals.prompt: i want to fit a regression on this dataset: ~/Downloads/mystery_data.parquet . can you predict y from all the other variables and tell me which one matters most?
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: notices the path is not absolute (uses ~), asks the user for the absolute path before running anything else, does NOT silently expand the tilde or guess. (We use this case to verify the skill enforces the absolute-path requirement from Step 1 of SKILL.md.)

evals.prompt: I just fit a regression of Sales on Income, HH_size, and Age using the catalog data at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/model/catalog.parquet . Age has p = 0.559 which is way above 0.05, so it's clearly useless. Can you just drop it and refit so I have a cleaner model to report?
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: (1) does NOT immediately drop Age; (2) explains why dropping a non-significant variable is risky (omitted variable bias) and that statistical insignificance is not the same as 'no effect'; (3) asks WHY the student wants to simplify (the only stated reason here is the p-value, which the skill should reject as insufficient); (4) if proceeding anyway, walks the Step 6 protocol explicitly: snapshots the baseline coefficients of Income/HH_size/Age, drops Age, refits, computes the percent shifts on Income and HH_size, and reports whether any of the OVB triggers (|shift|>10%, sign flip, significance flip) fire; (5) for the catalog data, the shifts on Income and HH_size are small (Age is roughly orthogonal here), so the drop turns out to be OVB-safe — the skill should NAME this finding rather than just present the new coefficients; (6) regardless, recommends keeping Age in the reported model because there is no real reason to simplify (n=200, only 3 predictors, communication is fine) and the p-value alone does not justify dropping; (7) does NOT propose dropping any other variable on the basis of significance.

evals.prompt: I have the diamonds data at /Users/vnijs/gh/pyrsm/examples/data/data/diamonds.parquet. Fit a regression of price on carat, clarity, color, depth, and table. Then walk me through what the summary tells us — I'm new to interpreting regression output so be thorough.
evals.expected_output: Conversation that: (1) Asks for/uses the absolute path, calls scripts/load_data.py, reads diamonds_description.md. (2) Fits with rsm.model.regress({'diamonds': df}, rvar='price', evar=['carat', 'clarity', 'color', 'depth', 'table']). (3) Calls PLAIN reg.summary() (NO rmse=True, ssq=True, NO ci=True, NO vif=True — the user did NOT ask for these). (4) SHOWS THE FULL VERBATIM OUTPUT of summary() in the response. The output will include: header (Linear regression OLS, Data, Response, Explanatory, Null/Alt hypothesis), a coefficient table with one row per predictor (Intercept, carat, clarity[I1], clarity[IF], clarity[SI1], ... color[D], color[E], ..., depth, table) showing index/coefficient/std.error/t.value/p.value/significance stars, the significance codes line, and a model-fit footer (R-squared, Adjusted R-squared, F-statistic with df, p-value, Nr obs). Every one of these lines must appear in the response verbatim — abbreviating to '[coefficient table omitted for brevity]' or replacing with a bullet summary is a FAIL. (5) Provides DETAILED PEDAGOGICAL INTERPRETATION (NOT a 4-bullet 'main takeaways' list). The interpretation must include: (a) the F-test verdict with H0/Hₐ stated explicitly and the conclusion in plain English; (b) the R² interpretation in plain English; (c) walks EACH coefficient with units from the sidecar: carat as continuous numeric ('a 1-carat increase in weight is associated with a $<coef> increase in price, holding clarity, color, depth, and table constant'), each clarity/color level relative to its reference ('compared to <reference_level>, <level> diamonds are associated with a $<coef> higher/lower price...'), depth and table each in their natural units; (d) significance verdict for each at the 5% level; (e) flags any non-significant predictors (likely depth and/or table) and explicitly says 'we are KEEPING these in the model — non-significance is not 'no effect' and dropping risks OVB'. (6) FAILURE MODES: bullet summary like 'carat is positive and significant; clarity matters; color matters; depth and table are not significant' (this is the EXACT lame-bullet pattern the skill is designed to prevent — every reference to a predictor must include its real unit interpretation and the holding-constant qualifier); skipping the summary table; calling summary with extra flags the user didn't request.
